summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history including sclerosing mesenteritis, multiple abdominal surgeries, and chronic anemia was admitted for vomiting, diarrhea, and new-onset bright red blood per rectum. Her hemoglobin had progressively dropped from 8.5 to 7.4 g/dL, prompting admission. Stool studies were negative for infection, and an abdominal X-ray showed dilated bowel loops without obstruction. A flexible sigmoidoscopy revealed no active bleeding source or ulcers, with findings suggesting resolved rectal lesions. Despite IV iron infusion, her hemoglobin continued to decline, necessitating transfusion of 2 units of packed red blood cells, after which her levels stabilized at 9.0 g/dL. Pain was managed conservatively due to prior sedation with opioids. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient GI follow-up, including possible capsule endoscopy, and instructions to monitor for recurrent bleeding.
